summary: Larry Ellison co-founded Oracle in 1977 and remains its executive chairman and chief technology officer. His political influence now extends beyond disclosed Republican contributions: Oracle is a major government technology provider, he cultivated a relationship with Donald Trump, and his capital backs family-controlled investments in Paramount, TikTok's U.S. operations and other media assets.

statements.summary: Ellison argued that customers should be able to use Oracle databases across multiple competing cloud platforms rather than be locked into one provider.
He presented unified data, identity and network controls as necessary to make cloud systems secure.
Ellison said hosting the fundraiser did not mean Oracle as a company endorsed Trump and noted that he did not personally attend.
Ellison and Oracle presented the company as a trusted technology partner capable of securing TikTok's U.S. data.
Ellison argued that large-scale AI infrastructure could accelerate personalized cancer detection and vaccine development.

chapters.title: An adopted child becomes a programmer
chapters.body:
Larry Ellison was born in New York in 1944 and raised in Chicago by his aunt and uncle. He attended two universities without graduating, then moved to California and worked in programming [[britannica-ellison, time-ellison-2024]].

His early career coincided with the emergence of relational databases, a technical opening he turned into a commercial project [[britannica-ellison]].

chapters.title: Building Oracle
chapters.dek: Database software creates one of technology's largest fortunes
chapters.body:
Ellison and two partners founded Oracle's predecessor in 1977. Government and corporate database contracts drove growth, and the company went public in 1986 [[oracle-bio, britannica-ellison]].

He served as CEO until 2014 and remains executive chairman and CTO. Oracle's 2026 proxy shows a founder stake near forty percent, tying most of his wealth directly to the company [[oracle-proxy-2026, forbes-ellison-2026]].

chapters.title: From centrist identity to Republican access
chapters.dek: Fundraisers, super PACs and a contested-election call
chapters.body:
Ellison has described himself as centrist, but recent disclosed giving favors Republicans. He hosted a 2020 Trump fundraiser and later joined a call discussing legal challenges to Trump's defeat [[time-fundraiser-2020, wapo-election-call-2022]].

About $30 million to Opportunity Matters Fund made a super PAC his largest disclosed vehicle. A separately reported $45 million nonprofit gift in 2024 remains unconfirmed by public filings and is labeled accordingly [[fec-ellison, fortune-darkmoney-2026]].

chapters.title: Technology peers and family capital
chapters.dek: Musk, Tesla and the next Ellison generation
chapters.body:
Ellison served on Tesla's board and invested $1 billion in Elon Musk's Twitter acquisition. Those ties connect him to another technology owner active in Republican politics [[tesla-proxy-2019, vanityfair-ellison-2026]].

His children David and Megan built film businesses. Larry's capital has been especially important to David's Skydance, making family finance a bridge from enterprise software into entertainment and news [[ap-warner-2025, axios-media-2026]].

chapters.title: Government technology as power
chapters.body:
Oracle sells database and cloud services to government agencies, making Ellison's policy access relevant even when no campaign contribution is involved [[oracle-proxy-2026, vanityfair-ellison-2026]].

At the 2025 White House launch of Stargate, Ellison joined Trump and other executives to promise large AI-infrastructure investment. The project joined commercial ambition to national industrial policy [[whitehouse-stargate-2025]].

chapters.title: Two attempts at TikTok
chapters.body:
Oracle first emerged as Trump's preferred TikTok partner in 2020, but that transaction did not close. The overlap between Ellison's political relationship and Oracle's bid drew scrutiny without proving improper intervention [[forbes-tiktok-2020]].

In 2025 an Oracle-led U.S. consortium gained a role in TikTok's American operations. Oracle's infrastructure responsibilities gave Ellison influence over a platform central to speech, commerce and national-security debates [[oracle-tiktok-2025, vanityfair-ellison-2026]].

chapters.title: A family-backed media empire
chapters.body:
Ellison financing enabled Skydance's Paramount acquisition and a later bid for Warner Bros. Discovery. A personal $40.4 billion guarantee showed that the expansion depended on Larry's balance sheet as well as David's management [[ap-warner-2025, axios-media-2026]].

The deals brought political scrutiny after Paramount settled Trump's lawsuit and regulators approved the merger. Reporting documents meetings and contested perceptions but does not establish a quid pro quo by Larry Ellison [[atlantic-paramount-2026, axios-media-2026]].

chapters.title: Present influence
chapters.dek: Oracle ownership meets media and political power
chapters.body:
At eighty-two, Ellison remains Oracle's executive chairman and CTO and one of its dominant shareholders. His fortune gives him capacity to finance transactions larger than his disclosed political ledger [[oracle-bio, oracle-proxy-2026, forbes-ellison-2026]].

By late 2026 his influence spanned Oracle, Stargate, TikTok U.S. and family-backed Paramount. The same breadth requires careful attribution: Oracle actions, David Ellison's editorial decisions and Larry Ellison's personal donations are related but not interchangeable [[vanityfair-ellison-2026, axios-media-2026]].
